items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the agriculture and markets law and the real property law, in relation to agricultural disclosure requirements for agricultural districts
items.lawCode: Amd §§308 & 310, Ag & Mkts L; amd §§333 & 333-c, RP L
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S1507

 TITLE OF BILL :

An act to amend the agriculture and markets law and the real property
law, in relation to agricultural disclosure requirements for
agricultural districts

 PURPOSE :

To notify prospective purchasers of real property that is in close
proximity to farm operations conducted in an agricultural district
about environmental impacts of such operations and the state's right
to farm policy.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

The bill amends sections 308 and 310 of the agricultural and markets
law, and sections 333 and 333c of the real property law to include
notification by grantors to prospective purchasers of real property
within five hundred feet of the boundary of an agricultural district
of their proximity to farm operations and associated environmental
impacts.

 JUSTIFICATION :

Increasingly, people are seeking to move to "the country", often near
farm operations, making it more important than ever to notify
prospective purchasers about the nature of farm operations, including
the sights, smells, sounds, and dust that may impact property in close
proximity to such operations.

Under current law, when a person seeks to purchase land "partially or
wholly within an agricultural district", they are given advance notice
(a disclosure notice) that some or all of the property lies within
such a district and are urged to contact the NYS state Department of
Agriculture and Markets for additional information about farm
operations conducted in agricultural districts.

This bill seeks to extend that notice to those prospective purchasers
of property within five hundred feet of the boundary of an
agricultural district, rather than limiting such notice to property
directly or partially within such a district. This will further serve
the intent of the current statutory language which is to increase
awareness of those seeking to purchase real property that is near an
agricultural district on the facts of farm operations and the state's
right to farm policy.

In addition, there is precedence in New York state law for using five
hundred feet as a measure. Chapter 658 of the laws of 2005, also a
Rural Resources Commission bill, required that municipalities provide
notice to their neighbors when undertaking certain planning and zoning
actions within five hundred feet of a neighboring municipality.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

2013-14: A1393 (Gunther) passed Assembly/S3860 (Ranzenhofer) referred
to Agriculture
2011-12: A5825 (Gunther) passed Assembly
2009-10: A7835 (Koon) passed Assembly/S5428 (Aubertine) referred to
Agriculture
2007-08: A 1 0169A (Koon) passed Assembly/S706 1 A (Winner) committed
to Rules

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

None.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect immediately.

summary: Requires purchasers of real property within 500 feet of the boundary of an agricultural district to be provided with disclosure of farming activities within such district.
title: Requires purchasers of real property within 500 feet of an agricultural district to be provided with disclosure of farming activities within such district
